edits.text: 2. COMPENSATION. The Executive shall receive an annual base salary of [AMOUNT SUBJECT TO CLIENT INSTRUCTIONS] (the “Base Salary”), payable in accordance with the Company’s regular payroll practices. The Executive shall be eligible to participate in the health, welfare and retirement benefit plans generally available to similarly situated executives, subject to applicable plan terms, and shall receive paid time off under the Company’s applicable executive policy. These proposals remain subject to client approval.

3. SEVERANCE. As a discussion proposal subject to client approval, upon termination by the Company without Cause, the Executive shall receive an amount equal to twelve months of the Executive’s then-current Base Salary (the “Severance Amount”), payable in substantially equal installments over twelve months, and, if continuation coverage is timely elected and legally available, reimbursement of the employer portion of health coverage premiums for up to twelve months, ending earlier upon eligibility for comparable coverage through another employer. Severance shall be conditioned on execution and non-revocation of a mutually acceptable release of claims and continued compliance with enforceable confidentiality and return-of-property obligations. Accrued salary, vested benefits and reimbursable business expenses shall remain payable independently of the release. The definition of Cause, release timing, payment commencement and applicable tax-compliance provisions remain to be agreed.

4. NON-COMPETE. [UNRESOLVED: The proposed twelve-month post-employment non-compete remains subject to agreement on restricted activities, geographic scope, applicable-law limitations, compensation and termination protections. No final agreement on this restriction is reflected in this draft.]

receiver.message_back: The package remains incomplete without a firm Base Salary proposal; please provide that figure, and revise severance to cover resignation for defined Good Reason as well as termination without narrowly defined Cause, with clear payment deadlines and no release condition on accrued entitlements. Our counterproposal deletes the non-compete; any narrowly tailored, legally enforceable restriction would require separately agreed compensation and termination protections, and all terms remain subject to our client’s approval.
